w:r.w:t: This Business Requirements Document (BRD) defines the functional and data requirements for Taara — a web-based Stock, Order, and Sales Management System for a single garment/apparel manufacturing business. The document serves as the authoritative reference for all design, development, and testing activities.

The client operates a garment manufacturing business that procures raw yarn, sends it to an external spinning factory, receives spun fabric back in-house, processes it through cutting and stitching stages, and maintains stock at each stage. The current process is manual, leading to stock discrepancies and a lack of visibility across stages.
Master Data Management (Styles, Dia, Stitching Sections)
The following are explicitly out of scope for Phase 1 but are designed for future extension:
A named combination of one or more colors of yarn. Defined in Master Data and used as a primary stock identifier throughout the system.
Diameter of the knitting machine gauge (e.g., 14dia, 16dia). Determines the fabric structure and is a key stock identifier from the In-house stage onward.
A named stitching unit — either an internal team or an external contractor — to whom cut garment pieces are dispatched for stitching.
A purchase order placed for raw yarn, tracked by Color and quantity in kgs.
The external factory process that converts raw yarn into knitted fabric. Tracked in kgs. The output is mapped to a Style at delivery time.
The physical process of cutting knitted fabric (tracked by Dia + Style in kgs) into individual garment pieces (tracked in pcs).
Finished pieces returned after stitching. Added to In-house stitched stock inventory.
Pieces returned from stitching that fall short of the ordered count. Tracked separately in In-house for visibility.
A user-defined kg adjustment applied at the spinning delivery stage to account for minor weight variances in spun output.
The diagram below represents the end-to-end production and stock flow across all modules:
Yarn Order (kgs, Color) → Spinning Factory (kgs) → In-house Delivery (kgs)
Split into Stock (Dia + Style, kgs) → Cutting (kgs → pcs) → Stitching Order (Style, pcs)
Stitching Delivery (pcs) → Stitched Stock (pcs) + Defective Stock (pcs)
Yarn → Spinning → In-house Delivery: tracked in kgs
In-house Stock (split): tracked in kgs by Dia + Style
Cutting: input in kgs (reduces Dia+Style stock), output in pcs
Stitching onwards: tracked in pcs by Style
The Master Data module provides the foundational reference data used across all other modules. It must be set up before any other module is used.
A Style is a named yarn composition — it represents a combination of colors that will be produced after spinning. Style is used as a primary identifier in stock, cutting, and stitching.
One or more colors associated with this style
A Style can have one or more colors associated with it.
A Style cannot be deleted if it is referenced in any stock, cutting, or stitching record.
Dia represents the knitting machine gauge diameter (e.g., 14dia, 16dia). It is used from the In-house splitting stage through cutting.
A Dia cannot be deleted if referenced in any stock or cutting record. Soft delete only.
A Stitching Section is a named stitching unit — either an in-house team or an external contractor — to which cut pieces are dispatched for stitching.
Unique name of the stitching unit
Identifies if this is in-house or contractor
A Section cannot be deleted if it has associated stitching orders.
Count of active dia values defined

This module tracks the procurement of raw yarn. Yarn is ordered by Style (which encapsulates color) and tracked in kgs. Each order entry also automatically creates a corresponding Spinning entry, since all ordered yarn is sent to the spinning factory.
Style (encapsulates color) of yarn being ordered
Quantity of yarn ordered in kgs
Each record represents a single yarn style/color order.
On saving a Yarn Order, a Spinning entry is automatically created with the same Style and kgs. The user is notified of this auto-creation.
Users can also create Spinning entries manually, independent of a Yarn Order (e.g., for yarn already at the factory without a formal order record).
Yarn Order records support soft delete only — no hard deletion allowed.
The yarn stock is a derived, running ledger. It tracks:
Total kgs ordered per Style (from all yarn order entries)
Total kgs dispatched to spinning per Style
The Yarn Orders list must support:
Filter by: Style, Date Range (Order Date)
Sort by: Order Date, Quantity (kgs), Style
KPI cards on the dashboard must update to reflect the current filter selection.
Total kgs ordered across all styles (filtered)
kgs ordered but not yet dispatched to spinning

This module tracks yarn sent to the external spinning factory and the delivery of spun fabric back to the business. It has two independent sections: Orders and Deliveries. There is NO mandatory link between a Spinning Order and a Spinning Delivery — deliveries can come in parts and are not tied 1:1 to orders.
A Spinning Order entry represents a batch of yarn dispatched to the spinning factory. Entries can be auto-created from a Yarn Order or added manually.
User-entered date yarn was sent to factory
Optional — auto-populated if created from Yarn Order; blank for manual entries
Style of yarn dispatched (same as Yarn Order Style when auto-created)
Optional name of spinning factory or remarks
When a Yarn Order is saved, a Spinning Order is auto-created with the same Style and kgs. The Linked Yarn Order field is populated automatically.
A user may also create a Spinning Order manually (Linked Yarn Order left blank).
No status field is maintained on Spinning Orders — stock tracking via kgs in/out is sufficient.

A Spinning Delivery entry records spun fabric received back from the factory. Deliveries are independent records — they are NOT linked to a specific Spinning Order. A delivery may represent a partial or full return of any previously dispatched yarn. The user maps the received fabric to a Style at delivery time and may apply a buffer to round off kgs.
Style mapped to the received spun fabric (same concept as color/style in yarn order)
Actual kgs of spun fabric received
User-entered +/- adjustment to round off final kgs
Style in Spinning Delivery and Style in Yarn Order are the same master reference — they represent the same concept (color/style combination). No separate color field exists.
On saving a Spinning Delivery, an In-house Delivery entry is auto-created using the Final Quantity and the mapped Style.
The Buffer field only affects the Final Quantity passed to In-house — it does not alter Spinning Order records.
Multiple Spinning Deliveries can be created over time as partial deliveries arrive. There is no cap per style or order.But the
delivery should not exceed the order
Filter by: Style, Date Range, Linked Yarn Order (Yes/No — manual vs auto)
Sort by: Dispatch Date, Quantity Sent, Style
Sort by: Delivery Date, Final Quantity, Style
KPI cards must update to reflect the current filter selection.
Total kgs sent across all spinning orders (filtered)
Total final kgs across all spinning deliveries (filtered)
Total Dispatched minus Total Received (overall, not filtered)
The In-house module is the central stock management module. It has four sections: Deliveries, Stock, Cutting, and Stitched Stock.
This section receives auto-created entries from Spinning Deliveries. The user cannot manually create entries here. It displays all deliveries received from spinning with their Style and kgs.
Enum: Pending / Partially Split / Fully Split
Tracks how much has been split into stock
From each Delivery entry, the user can split the kgs into one or more Stock entries (see Stock section below).
Stitching stock represents the available in-house
fabric inventory, identified by Dia + Style in kgs. Stock entries are created by splitting a Delivery entry.
Split Entry fields (created per split action from a Delivery):
kgs allocated to this Dia+Style split
The sum of all split quantities for a Delivery entry must not exceed the Delivery's total kgs.
Each split entry adds to the running stock for that Dia + Style combination.
A Delivery entry can be split multiple times until its full kgs are allocated.
Live stock for any Dia + Style = Sum of all split kgs − Sum of all cutting kgs for that Dia + Style.

Cutting records the physical process of cutting fabric into garment pieces. A cutting entry is a two-step process: the user first enters the kgs taken from stock (which immediately reduces stock), then later updates the same record to add the pieces produced.
kgs taken from stock — stock reduced immediately on save
Number of garment pieces produced — filled in a subsequent update
In-Progress when only kgs entered; Completed when pcs are also entered
BLOCKING VALIDATION: The system must block submission if Quantity Used (kgs) exceeds the current available stock for the selected Dia + Style.
Stock reduction happens immediately when the cutting entry is first saved with kgs — even before pcs are entered.
The user can return to an In-Progress cutting entry at any time to update Output Pieces (pcs).
Status is auto-set to 'In-Progress' when only kgs are saved; auto-updated to 'Completed' when pcs are also saved.
Cutting is also reportable by Dia only (aggregated) — total kgs cut per Dia regardless of style.
Soft delete only. If a cutting entry is soft-deleted, the kgs must be restored to stock.
Tracks final stitched garment pieces returned from the Stitching module. Entries are auto-created when a Stitching Delivery is confirmed.
Pieces accepted as good quality from this delivery
Calculated only when Stitching Order is marked Complete
Good Pieces are added per delivery entry as they arrive (partial deliveries supported).
Defective Pieces = Ordered Pieces (for the Stitching Order) minus Total Good Pieces delivered across ALL deliveries for that order.
Defective Pieces are only calculated and recorded when the user manually marks the Stitching Order as 'Complete'.
Defective pieces are stored for visibility only — no further workflow action in Phase 1.
Deliveries list: Filter by Style, Date Range; Sort by Date, kgs, Style.
Stock list: Filter by Dia, Style; Sort by kgs (ascending/descending), Dia, Style.
Cutting list: Filter by Dia, Style, Status (In-Progress / Completed), Date Range; Sort by Date, kgs, pcs, Dia, Style.
Stitched Stock list: Filter by Style, Date Range; Sort by Good Pieces, Defective Pieces.
KPI cards must update to reflect the current filter selection on each section.
Total kgs across all Dia+Style combos
Total kgs cut per Dia across all styles
Count of cutting entries with status In-Progress
Total pcs produced from all completed cutting entries
Total good pcs in stitched inventory by Style
Total defective pcs accumulated by Style

The Stitching module tracks garment pieces sent out for stitching and the return of stitched pieces. It has two sections: Orders and Deliveries. A Stitching Order can have multiple partial deliveries. Defective pieces are only calculated when the order is manually marked as Complete.
A Stitching Order records cut pieces dispatched to a Stitching Section.
User-entered date the order was placed
Style of garment pieces being sent
Number of pieces dispatched for stitching
User manually updates this field; not auto-calculated
Status defaults to 'Pending' on creation. The user manually changes it to 'Partially Delivered' or 'Complete' as appropriate.
Defective pieces are calculated ONLY when the user marks the order Status as 'Complete' (see Stitched Stock in In-house module).
One Stitching Order can receive multiple Stitching Delivery entries over time.
A Stitching Delivery records stitched pieces returned from a Stitching Section, linked to a Stitching Order. Multiple deliveries can be made against a single order.
Actual pieces returned in this delivery
WARNING VALIDATION: If the cumulative Pieces Delivered across all deliveries for a Stitching Order exceeds Pieces Ordered, the system displays a warning (but allows saving after acknowledgment).
On saving a Stitching Delivery, an In-house Stitched Stock entry is auto-created with the Pieces Delivered for this delivery as Good Pieces.

Defective Pieces are NOT calculated per delivery. They are calculated only when the Stitching Order is marked Complete: Defective = Ordered Pieces − Total Good Pieces across all deliveries for that order.
Stitching Orders list: Filter by Style, Section, Status, Date Range; Sort by Date, Pieces Ordered, Status, Section.
Stitching Deliveries list: Filter by Linked Order, Style, Section, Date Range; Sort by Date, Pieces Delivered.
KPI cards must update to reflect the current filter selection.
Pcs from all Pending/Partially Delivered orders (filtered)
Total pcs returned across all deliveries (filtered)
Count of orders with Pending status
Count of orders with Partially Delivered status
Total defective pcs from all Completed orders
Breakdown of pending pcs per stitching section
The following rules govern how stock is calculated at each stage. These are non-negotiable and must be validated in both UI and backend logic.
Ordered kgs − Dispatched to Spinning kgs
Total Dispatched kgs − Total Delivered kgs (across all deliveries, all styles)
Auto-created from Spinning Delivery Final Quantity
Sum of Split kgs − Sum of Cutting kgs used (per Dia+Style)
Pieces recorded per cutting entry (after update)
Ordered pcs − Sum of all Delivered pcs (per order)
Sum of Good Pieces from all stitching deliveries
Ordered pcs − Total Delivered pcs (calculated only on Order Completion)
BLOCK: Cutting Quantity (kgs) > Available Stock for Dia + Style — entry is rejected
WARN: Cumulative Stitching Delivery pcs > Stitching Order pcs — warning shown, user must acknowledge to proceed
INFO: Spinning Delivery quantity differs significantly from any single Spinning Order qty — for user awareness only
If a Cutting entry is soft-deleted, the kgs used must be restored to the Dia + Style stock immediately.
If an In-house Stock split is soft-deleted, the split kgs are removed from stock.
If a Stitching Delivery is soft-deleted, the Good Pieces are removed from Stitched Stock.
Every module must maintain a full, immutable transaction history. The owner must be able to see both the current live stock levels and all historical entries that contributed to those levels.
All entries (yarn orders, spinning dispatches, deliveries, splits, cuttings, stitching orders, stitching deliveries) must be permanently stored and visible in list views.
No record should be permanently deleted — a soft-delete or archive mechanism is preferred.
Each module's list screen must show all transactions with sortable date columns.
The stock calculation at any point must be fully derivable from the transaction history.
Each main module follows a consistent structure:
Dashboard Screen: KPI cards showing live stock numbers for that module.
List Screen: A tabular list of all records with key fields visible, sortable by date.
Detail / Entry Screen: Full record view with all fields, action buttons, and linked records.
Dashboard | Deliveries | Stock | Cutting | Stitched Stock
Spinning Delivery → auto-creates In-house Delivery entry (user is notified/redirected).
In-house Delivery → user initiates 'Split' action → creates one or more Stock entries.
In-house Cutting → Dia+Style stock selector shows available kgs in real-time; blocks if insufficient.
Stitching Delivery → auto-creates Stitched Stock and Defective Stock entries in In-house.
Must be responsive enough for desktop use.
Single user — no multi-user or role-based access in Phase 1.

The following table summarises all entities, their key identifiers, and relationships. Every entity includes: AutoId (auto-increment human-readable), id (UUID primary key), isDeleted (soft delete flag), createdAt, and updatedAt as standard system fields.
Referenced by: Yarn Order, Spinning Order, Spinning Delivery, In-house Stock, Cutting, Stitching Order
Referenced by: In-house Stock splits, Cutting
Referenced by: Stitching Order, Stitching Delivery
Optional link → Yarn Order; No link to Spinning Delivery (deliveries are independent)
No mandatory link to Spinning Order; 1:1 → In-house Delivery (auto-created)
Derived: Sum of Split kgs − Sum of Cutting kgs per Dia+Style
References Dia, Style; reduces In-house Stock immediately on save (kgs). Two-step: kgs first, pcs later.
References Section, Style; 1:many → Stitching Deliveries. Status is user-editable.
Many:1 → Stitching Order; auto-creates In-house Stitched Stock entry per delivery
Good pcs added per delivery. Defective pcs calculated only when Stitching Order is marked Complete.
Are there additional details needed per stitching order or delivery beyond what is specified (e.g., rate per piece, delivery challan number)?
Is there a need to track which specific In-house Stock entry (Dia+Style, kgs) was used for which Stitching Order? Currently not in scope.
Buffer/round-off is confirmed at Spinning Delivery. Are there any other stages where kgs adjustment is needed?
Sales, Dispatch, Labelling, Packaging, QC — to be scoped in Phase 2.
All users of the system are the business owner or authorized manager — no role-based access control is required in Phase 1.
There is only one spinning factory in use at a time. Multi-factory support is not required.
Style encapsulates color — they are the same concept. Style is the master identifier used throughout the system; no separate Color field exists in stock or cutting.
All kgs values support up to 2 decimal places. All piece counts are whole integers.

AutoId fields are human-readable, auto-incrementing, prefixed per entity (e.g., YRN-001, SPO-001) and are separate from the UUID primary key. They may be used as display identifiers and future foreign key references.
createdAt and updatedAt are separate, independent DateTime fields on every entity.
All deletes across the system are soft deletes only — records are flagged with isDeleted = true and hidden from normal views but retained in the database.
When a soft-deleted record affects stock (e.g., a cutting entry), the stock impact must be reversed immediately.
The system does not need to integrate with any external ERP, accounting, or inventory system in Phase 1.
Data backup and security are the responsibility of the hosting infrastructure, not part of this BRD.
Sales, dispatch, and customer order management
Quality control workflows beyond defective piece count
Financial tracking (cost per kg, cost per piece, invoicing)
Advanced reporting and analytics beyond module dashboards
